Summary using Beige Book insights:
- Policy stance: The FOMC delivered a cautious 25 bp cut to 2.00–2.25%, lowered IOER to 2.10%, and ended balance-sheet runoff early, citing muted inflation and global developments while labor markets remain strong.
- Beige Book cross-check: District reports point to moderate overall growth with mixed sectoral performance—nonfinancial services generally stronger; manufacturing production flat; oil and gas and agriculture softer; commercial rents higher; transportation varied; nonresidential construction mixed. Labor markets remained tight with worker shortages. Trade-related uncertainty persisted.
- Credit conditions (SLOOS overlay): Banks tightened standards for C&I and construction/land development loans, with softer demand in that CRE segment; consumer lending largely unchanged. This supports the FOMC’s note that business fixed investment is soft and adds downside risk to capex.
- Implication: The rate cut and early end to runoff are supportive, but Beige Book and SLOOS evidence of tighter business credit and uneven activity temper the outlook. Net tone is cautiously positive but close to neutral.
